title: Compressor age and energy use
intro:
A plant logged the average daily energy use (kWh/day) of fourteen identical air compressors of different ages (years). Take x = age and y = energy use.

How well does a straight line describe the data? Find R², the residual standard error σ̂ (in kWh/day) and the ANOVA F statistic. Give R² to two decimals or more, σ̂ and F to two decimals.

To use the Workbench: press **Copy the data**, press Ctrl+B, click **+ Data table** and paste (Ctrl+V). Choose **Simple linear regression** in the list on the left, set **x column** to *Age (years)* and **y column** to *Energy (kWh/day)*. Read **R²**, **Residual standard error (σ̂)** and **ANOVA F**. Ctrl+L brings you back.

RSquared.says: That is r. R² is r squared, or SS regression / SS total.
That is the adjusted R². The question asks the plain R² = SS regression / SS total.

ResidualSe.says: That is the RMSE with n in the denominator, √(SS error / n). σ̂ divides by the error degrees of freedom, n − 2: σ̂ = √(SS error / (n − 2)).
That is σ̂², the mean square error. Take its square root.

FStatistic.says: That is the t statistic of the slope. In simple regression F = t².

hints: Fit the line first (b₁ = S_xy / S_xx, b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄), then the residuals eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ.
SS total = Σ(y − ȳ)², SS error = Σeᵢ², SS regression = SS total − SS error. R² = SS regression / SS total.
σ̂ = √(SS error / (n − 2)). F = (SS regression / 1) / (SS error / (n − 2)) on 1 and n − 2 degrees of freedom.
